title: Gestational diabetes mellitus (GDM): India DIPSI pathway
subject: obstetrics-gynaecology
setting: Antenatal clinic, PHC to district hospital, labour room
summary: Test every pregnant woman with a single-step 75 g oral glucose load, fasting or not; GDM if the 2-hour plasma glucose is 140 mg/dL (7.8 mmol/L) or more. Start MNT and exercise for 2 weeks, then add insulin (any gestation) or metformin (from 20 weeks) if 2-hour PPBS stays 120 mg/dL (6.7 mmol/L) or more.

sections.title: Screen and diagnose (MoHFW 2018)
items: Universal testing: at the first antenatal contact (as early as possible) and again at 24 to 28 weeks if the first test is negative, at least 4 weeks apart. If first seen after 28 weeks, test once at first contact.

Method: 75 g glucose dissolved in about 300 mL water, drunk within 5 to 10 minutes, whether fasting or not and irrespective of the last meal. Measure plasma glucose at 2 hours (plasma-calibrated glucometer acceptable). If she vomits within 30 minutes, repeat the next day.
GDM: 2-hour plasma glucose 140 mg/dL (7.8 mmol/L) or more.

Some laboratories use IADPSG/WHO 2013 fasting OGTT criteria (fasting 92, 1-hour 180, 2-hour 153 mg/dL; 5.1, 10.0, 8.5 mmol/L). Use one system consistently; this protocol follows the national DIPSI criterion.
Fasting glucose 126 mg/dL (7.0 mmol/L) or more, or 2-hour 200 mg/dL (11.1 mmol/L) or more, suggests diabetes predating pregnancy: manage as pre-existing diabetes with specialist input.

sections.title: First line: medical nutrition therapy (MNT) and exercise
items: Start MNT at diagnosis: carbohydrate-controlled, balanced meals spread as 3 meals and 2 to 3 snacks, using locally available foods; plus 30 minutes of walking or exercise daily.
After 2 weeks of MNT, check 2-hour post-meal plasma glucose (PPBS).
PPBS below 120 mg/dL (6.7 mmol/L): continue MNT and exercise; repeat FBS and PPBS at least monthly in the second and third trimesters, or as the treating doctor advises.
Targets: fasting below 95 mg/dL (5.3 mmol/L) and 2-hour post-meal below 120 mg/dL (6.7 mmol/L); ADA 2026 also accepts 1-hour post-meal below 140 mg/dL (7.8 mmol/L).

sections.title: Medication when MNT fails
items: PPBS 120 mg/dL or more after 2 weeks of MNT: add insulin or metformin to MNT.
Insulin is the drug of first choice (MoHFW, ADA 2026) and can be started at any gestation. Before 20 weeks use insulin only.

Metformin may be used from 20 weeks if MNT fails: 500 mg twice daily with meals, titrated to a maximum of 2 g/day. If targets are not met at the maximum dose, add insulin. It crosses the placenta and long-term offspring data are limited (ADA 2026).
MoHFW insulin start: human premix 30/70 subcutaneously 30 minutes before breakfast: 4 units if PPBS 120 to 160 mg/dL, 6 units if 160 to 200 mg/dL, 8 units if above 200 mg/dL.
Titrate every 3rd day on FBS and PPBS: add 2 units pre-breakfast if PPBS is raised, and give 2 units pre-dinner if FBS is raised, until FBS is below 95 mg/dL and PPBS below 120 mg/dL.

Refer to a higher centre if insulin exceeds 20 units/day, metformin needs more than 2 g/day, FBS is above 150 or PPBS above 250 mg/dL on treatment, PPBS is above 200 mg/dL at any time, hypoglycaemia occurs more than once a day, or insulin is refused.

Hypoglycaemia (below 70 mg/dL, 3.9 mmol/L): 15 to 20 g glucose (about 3 teaspoons of glucose powder) in water, rest, recheck, then a snack. Every woman on insulin should keep glucose or sugar at home.

sections.title: Antenatal monitoring
items: FBS and 2-hour PPBS every 3rd day while adjusting insulin (twice weekly while adjusting metformin), then at least monthly once stable.
Anomaly scan at 18 to 20 weeks if GDM was diagnosed before 20 weeks. Growth scans (biometry and liquor) at 28 to 30 weeks and 34 to 36 weeks.
At each visit look for macrosomia, growth restriction, polyhydramnios, hypertension and proteinuria; teach daily fetal movement counting.
If preterm birth is expected at 24 to 34 weeks, give dexamethasone 6 mg IM 12-hourly for 4 doses and monitor glucose closely for the next 72 hours, increasing insulin as needed.

sections.title: Labour, birth and the newborn
items: Well controlled (PPBS below 120 mg/dL): institutional birth at the local facility. Routine delivery before 39 weeks is not recommended; induce at or after 39 weeks if not delivered spontaneously.
Poor control, insulin above 20 units/day, or other complications: refer at 34 to 36 weeks to a CEmOC centre; earlier birth is individualised for poor control, hypertension or previous stillbirth.
Vaginal birth is preferred. Consider elective caesarean at 39 weeks if estimated fetal weight is above 4 kg (shoulder dystocia risk).

On the day of induction or labour, withhold the morning insulin or metformin, check capillary glucose 2-hourly, and start IV normal saline with regular insulin as per the MoHFW intrapartum table if glucose is raised.

Newborn: breastfeed within the first hour; check glucose at 1 hour and then before feeds every 4 hours until 4 stable values. Glucose below 45 mg/dL is hypoglycaemia: breastfeed immediately and follow the neonatal hypoglycaemia protocol.

sections.title: After birth: long-term follow-up
items: Most women need no glucose-lowering drugs after birth; stop insulin and metformin and encourage breastfeeding.

75 g OGTT (fasting and 2-hour) at 6 weeks postpartum (MoHFW; ADA 2026 allows 4 to 12 weeks) using non-pregnant criteria: diabetes if fasting 126 mg/dL (7.0 mmol/L) or more, or 2-hour 200 mg/dL (11.1 mmol/L) or more; impaired glucose tolerance if 2-hour 140 to 199 mg/dL (7.8 to 11.0 mmol/L).
Normal result: lifestyle advice, weight monitoring and exercise, with glucose screening every 1 to 3 years for life (ADA 2026; MoHFW advises annual screening at the NCD clinic).
Abnormal result: link to the NCD programme. Prediabetes with overweight: intensive lifestyle measures and/or metformin (ADA 2026).
Counsel about the high lifetime risk of type 2 diabetes (about 50 to 60%), early testing in any future pregnancy, and healthy lifestyle for the child.

sections.title: Pitfalls
items: Sending women away because they are not fasting: the DIPSI test is done in the fed or fasting state.
Using a glucometer that is not plasma-calibrated, or letting her skip the 24 to 28 week repeat test after a negative early test.
Using HbA1c to diagnose GDM or for the postpartum check (it reads low in and just after pregnancy).
Starting metformin before 20 weeks, exceeding 2 g/day, or using sulfonylureas (more neonatal hypoglycaemia and macrosomia).
Missing neonatal hypoglycaemia, and failing to arrange the 6-week postpartum OGTT.

drugs.name: Human premix insulin 30/70
drugs.dose: Start 4, 6 or 8 units SC 30 minutes before breakfast (PPBS 120 to 160, 160 to 200, above 200 mg/dL); adjust by 2 units every 3rd day; split with a pre-dinner dose if FBS is raised
drugs.notes: MoHFW first-choice drug. Refer if more than 20 units/day. Use 40 IU/mL vials with 40 IU syringes.

drugs.name: Metformin
drugs.dose: 500 mg orally twice daily with meals, titrate to maximum 2 g/day
drugs.notes: Only from 20 weeks. Add insulin if targets not met. GI upset common.

drugs.name: Oral glucose (hypoglycaemia)
drugs.dose: 15 to 20 g glucose in water; repeat if still below 70 mg/dL after 15 minutes, then a snack
drugs.notes: Women on insulin should keep glucose or sugar at home.

drugs.name: Dexamethasone (if preterm birth expected)
drugs.dose: 6 mg IM every 12 hours for 4 doses
drugs.notes: 24 to 34 weeks. Expect hyperglycaemia for about 72 hours; increase monitoring and insulin.
